newsitem.title: USA: Dollar gains on hopes of higher U.S. interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Dollar gains on hopes of higher U.S. interest rates.

text.p: The dollar ended modestly higher Wednesday as profit-taking cut into the German mark and U.S. inflation data kept hopes alive for higher U.S. interest rates.
The data showed that retail prices rose by 0.3 percent in February, a trace higher than the 0.2 percent expected by economists.

Analysts said the report painted a picture of relatively subdued price gains, but said it was unlikely to dissuade Federal Reserve policy-makers from launching a pre-emptive strike against inflation by hiking interest rates when they meet next week.

"It's not a troublesome surge in inflation," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp. "But I don't think the Fed really needs anything much more than what they're seeing right now to raise rates."
A hike in U.S. interest rates would make dollar-denominated assets more attractive to foreign investors, and would therefore boost the dollar.
The dollar ended the day at 1.6810 marks, up from 1.6738 marks Tuesday. Against the yen, the dollar rose to 122.82 from 122.45.
Also helping the dollar Wednesday was weakness in the mark, which came under pressure after several days of gains.
The mark was heavily bought on Monday and Tuesday at the expense of the British pound amid concerns that Germany might not qualify on time for European monetary union.
But investors bought back sterling at the expense of the mark after surprisingly strong U.K. employment and retail sales figures highlighted the health of Britain's economy.
"That helped continue to push the mark lower pretty much across the board," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer and Co.
Dealers said the dollar's gains against the yen were more limited because of caution ahead of U.S. trade data due Thursday.

Many analysts expect the report to show a widening in the U.S. trade deficit with Japan. This could spur trade tensions between the two countries and result in calls for a weaker dollar to boost U.S. competitiveness.

"The trade data coming tomorrow is important," said Bob Lynch, senior currency analyst at MMS International. "Dollar/yen has had a nice rebound but with heightened sensitivity from U.S. officials on the trade data, that may have encouraged some profit-taking."
In other trading Wednesday, sterling closed at $1.5982, up from $1.5907. The dollar ended stronger at 1.4425 Swiss francs, up from Tuesday's close of 1.4390.
The dollar settled at Canadian $1.3774 versus C$1.3735.
